project.name: plalast
project.title: plalast - The Living Creature
project.purpose: The brain of this repo. Every .md in the repo root and in agents/ is generated from this file, with folders, symlinks and .gitignore: edit only this file (modules in agents/ subfolders are hand-written), then run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build`. See agents/BUILD.md.

keys.primary: Control panel: what to build and how.
keys.primary.project: Identity: `name`, `title`, `plalast_logo` (path of the project logo), `purpose`, `repository` and `branches`.
keys.primary.levers: Memory lever of every document section, as `<doc>` -> `<section id>` -> value (see Memory levers).
keys.primary.on_demand: Where `on_demand` sections go (`dir`), the heading of the pointer list (`heading`) and the pointer line (`pointer`, with `{path}`, `{title}` and `{when}`).
keys.primary.adapters: Per provider, which `agents/` folders get one symlink per module (`source`) and where (`dest`).
keys.primary.audit: Settings of `pla-audit`: `allow` (exact strings or repo paths that are never reported, such as a public contact email) and `max_file_kb` (larger files are reported).
keys.primary.schema: This documentation of the config format; `BUILD.md` renders its tables.
keys.data.structure: Every path, in order: `path`, `type`, `description`; optional `table` and `label` (its row in the Structure table), `gitkeep`, `secret`, `target` and `build`.
keys.data.content: One document per key: `head` (blocks before the first section) and `sections` (`id`, `title`, `when`, `blocks`). A `file` entry with `build: "<key>"` is rendered from it.

levers.enabled: Rendered inside its document as `## <title>`: always in the agent's memory.
levers.on_demand: Rendered to `<on_demand.dir>/<id>.md`; the document keeps only a pointer line under the on_demand heading, and the agent reads the file when `when` applies.

entry_types.dir: Creates the folder; `gitkeep: true` adds an empty `.gitkeep`; `secret: true` git-ignores its contents except `.gitkeep`.
entry_types.symlink: Creates a link to `target`, relative to the link's folder.
entry_types.file + build: Renders `data.content.<build>`; `build: "gitignore"` renders `.gitignore` from the secret and ignored entries.
entry_types.file + build: null: Hand-written code such as `Cargo.toml` or `src/`; never an `.md` in the root or `agents/`. Left as is.
entry_types.planned: Not created; listed as planned in the Structure table.

blocks.heading: `#` repeated `level` times, then `text`
blocks.structure_table: the Structure table, from the `data.structure` entries that have `table`
blocks.schema: a table of `primary.schema.<part>` with the given `header`
blocks.image: `![alt](src)`, or an HTML `` when `width` is set; `ref` (a dotted config path such as `primary.project.plalast_logo`) can replace `src`

head.text: This repo is a public and living creature. Turn on your VPS or machine, connect your agents, code it, teach it something, and make a pull request on Github.
The servers will be 24/7 on. This is a personal project on autonomous coding and living information systems, but everyone is welcome in.

sections.title: Best practices
sections.when: deciding how to write, format or place anything in the repo

items: Single source: `config.json` is the brain. Every `.md` in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from it, so edit only `config.json` and run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build` (see `agents/BUILD.md`). Modules in `agents/` subfolders are hand-written. Never edit generated files by hand.
Naming: when the user says "la memoria", "el contexto" or "el json" (memory, context, the json), they mean `config.json`.

File changes: when the user asks to touch any file, make the change in its section of `config.json` and rebuild with `pla-build` (the Rust build tool); never edit the output directly. Only the hand-written Rust code and the modules in `agents/` subfolders are edited in place.

Memory levers: every document section in `config.json` has a lever in `primary.levers`: `enabled` (always in the agent's memory), `on_demand` (its own file, read when needed) or `disabled` (not built). Every new section gets one.

Zettelkasten markdown spirit. A lot of things in the web are garbage, so notes in the agent-zettelkasten use CDU (Universal Decimal Classification) notation: the file name starts with the CDU code, then a kebab-case title, e.g. `004.8-llm-agents.md` (004.8 = artificial intelligence). The infrastructure will be up.
Specific formats: markdown for information, json for configs, bash for system scripts (setup, links, servers) and Rust for everything else (see Tools and languages).
No duplication. Only one way of functional working, only one config file, symbolic links where matters, only one zettelkasten vault, etc.
Using languages LLM-friendly like Rust, Python or Go is desirable. Also, using LLM programming-specific languages is a tool to proceed with caution, but desirable at some point.
Formal verification is desirable, but very expensive. Watch out and connect to others' ideas instead of reinventing the wheel
Open source: everyone can collaborate with it (see `README.md` at the repo root for the contribution flow)

sections.title: Commands
sections.when: building, testing or checking the repo

blocks.text: Repo tool (details in `agents/BUILD.md`), from anywhere inside the repo:

items: `cargo run --release --bin pla-build`: regenerate docs, folders and links from `config.json`
`cargo run --release --bin pla-build -- --check`: change nothing, fail if the repo drifted from `config.json`
`cargo run --release --bin pla-recall -- [term]`: print the repo map, or search it for `term`
`cargo run --release --bin pla-lint -- [config] [modules] [rust]`: check that config.json, the hand-written modules and the Rust code are well formed
`cargo run --release --bin pla-audit -- [secrets] [deps] [repo]`: look for secrets and personal data, vulnerable dependencies, broken links and branches out of sync
Rust: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo test <test_name>` (single test), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
Verus: `verus <file>.rs`
Lean 4: `lake build`
Dafny: `dafny verify <file>.dfy`

head.text: A public, living repository on autonomous coding and living information systems. Servers run 24/7; anyone can connect their agents, teach it something and open a pull request.
Project rules and conventions for humans and agents: [agents/AGENTS.md](agents/AGENTS.md). Everything is generated from [config.json](config.json); see [agents/BUILD.md](agents/BUILD.md).

sections.title: Contributing
sections.when: preparing a branch or a pull request

items: Fork the repo and create a branch from `develop` (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`, `docs/<topic>`).

Change only `config.json` (or a hand-written module in an `agents/` subfolder), run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build`, and keep each change small: no duplication, Rust by default, markdown/json/bash formats.
Run `pla-lint` and `pla-audit` (see *Commands* in agents/AGENTS.md): both must finish with no errors.
Open a pull request against `develop` describing what changed and why. `main` only receives merges from `develop`.

head.text: `config.json` is the brain of this repo: every `.md` file in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from it, together with folders, symlinks and `.gitignore`. Modules in the `agents/` subfolders (skills, subagents, rules, hooks, mcp, memory) are hand-written and are not generated. Never edit a generated file: edit `config.json` and rebuild.

rows: Builds the repo from `config.json`. Idempotent: only writes what changed.
Changes nothing; exits non-zero if the repo drifted from `config.json` (stale file, missing link, stray `.md`).
Prints the map: every path in `structure` with its type and description.
Searches paths, descriptions and document text for `<term>` (case-insensitive), naming the file and section of each hit.

Checks that `config.json` is consistent and fully documented in `primary.schema`, that hand-written modules have the right shape (skill folders with `SKILL.md`, frontmatter `name` and `description`), and that `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` pass. Pass `config`, `modules` or `rust` to run only some areas.

Looks for keys, tokens, emails and home-folder paths in what git would commit, files committed inside secret folders, known vulnerabilities in `Cargo.lock` (with `cargo-audit`), broken links, large files, uncommitted changes and branches out of sync. Pass `secrets`, `deps` or `repo` to run only some areas; `primary.audit` holds its settings.

blocks.text: Run them from anywhere inside the repo: the tool walks up to the folder that holds `config.json`. Symlinks need a Unix system (Linux or macOS). `pla-build` never replaces a real file or folder with a link, and never deletes anything except broken adapter links.
It has exactly two top-level keys: `primary`, the control panel (what to build and how), and `data`, what gets built. Any other top-level key is an error.

sections.title: Memory levers
sections.when: changing what agents load into memory

blocks.text: Every section of every document has a lever in `primary.levers.<doc>.<section id>`. A missing lever, a lever for a section that does not exist, or a value outside this table stops the build.
Switching a section from `on_demand` to `disabled` leaves its old file behind: `pla-build` reports it as a stray `.md` and fails until you delete it.

sections.title: Structure entry types
sections.when: adding or changing a path in data.structure

blocks.text: Each section is rendered as `## <title>` followed by its blocks. Blocks are separated by one blank line and every file ends with one newline.

sections.title: Adding a module
sections.when: adding a skill, subagent or rule

blocks.text: Write the module in its folder (for example `agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and run `pla-build`: each adapter links it on its own (`.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../agents/skills/<name>`), never a whole folder. Links of deleted modules are removed on the next build.

Deleting an entry from `config.json` does not delete it from disk. `pla-build --check` reports leftover `.md` files in the root and `agents/`; delete them once you have confirmed they are no longer needed.
